raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`Zigzag PCP` splits each request's local queries into early and late segments. `FlashAttention` currently runs them separately, requiring two attention launches and an output concatenation per layer. Its varlen API already supports separate batch entries with independent KV lengths.

## Modifications

- Dispatch both segments in one varlen attention call using the existing combined zigzag metadata.
- Duplicate page-table rows once per forward batch and reuse them across layers, including the sliding-window page table where applicable.
- Remove the unused `cu_seqlens_k_new` argument from the CP callbacks; these calls read the KV cache without appending K/V.
- Keep the TRT-LLM-specific arguments and restore any padded output rows.
- Add a dispatch regression test and update CP strategy tests for the combined geometry.

## Accuracy Tests

4×H200; TP4, zigzag PCP4, EP4, FA3, BF16, page size 64.

DeepSeek-V2-Lite and GLM-4.7-Flash: deterministic inference, input lengths 8K/32K/64K, output lengths 1/16, 20 measured responses per case. **240/240 paired responses have identical text, generated token IDs and output logprobs (maximum absolute difference 0).** These are synthetic-input consistency checks, not task-accuracy evaluations.

GLM-4.7-Flash also matches exactly across all 240 ordinary-mode paired responses. V2-Lite also matches exactly across all 120 ordinary-mode paired responses.

Additional V2-Lite deterministic checks cover ragged batches `[17, 65, 513]` and `[2049, 4099]`, a 32K cached prefix followed by a 257-token suffix, and a cached ragged batch with 129/513-token suffixes. The prefix-hit requests report 32,768 cached tokens. All outputs and output logprobs match exactly. The separately profiled cold 32K/1 request also matches exactly.

CP strategy and MLA dispatch tests: **25 tests and 20 subtests passed**. Pre-commit passed for the five modified files.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Baseline `ed0b8f433f`; candidate `ccf5fe53`. DeepSeek-V2-Lite uses one baseline/candidate pair. GLM-4.7-Flash uses four independent engine starts: baseline → candidate → candidate → baseline; its second pair reverses case order. Each case has 4 warmups and 20 measured requests. Prefix cache disabled, concurrency 1, DeepEP BF16 dispatch and DeepGEMM. Entries below show the reduction in median server end-to-end latency; positive is faster. V2-Lite entries show its one pair and absolute baseline → candidate times. GLM entries show pair 1 / pair 2.

| Model | Input | Output 1 | Output 16 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | 8K | +3.15% (79.83 → 77.31 ms) | +2.23% (140.26 → 137.13 ms) |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | 32K | +1.13% (338.52 → 334.69 ms) | +0.81% (398.96 → 395.73 ms) |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | 64K | +0.99% (1092.46 → 1081.63 ms) | +1.40% (1172.06 → 1155.69 ms) |
| GLM-4.7-Flash | 8K | +2.09% / +3.06% | +0.48% / +1.71% |
| GLM-4.7-Flash | 32K | +1.15% / +1.48% | +1.86% / +2.75% |
| GLM-4.7-Flash | 64K | +1.94% / +1.82% | +1.33% / +1.80% |

Separate Nsight Systems captures of a cold V2-Lite 32K/1 request confirm **54 → 27 FlashAttention kernels on every GPU**, matching 27 layers with two → one launches per layer. 

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A: internal dispatch optimization; no user-facing behavior or configuration change.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@Fridge003 This PR extends the single-call zigzag attention approach from #33137 to the FlashAttention backend, reusing the combined metadata you introduced. We validated it with FA3 on DeepSeek-V2-Lite and GLM-4.7-Flash, including output consistency checks and an Nsight trace confirming two attention launches per layer become one.

+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.flashattention_backend import (
+    FlashAttentionBackend,
+    FlashAttentionMetadata,
+)
+from sglang.srt.layers.cp.zigzag import ZigzagCPStrategy
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_batch_info import ForwardMode
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_parallel
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+MODULE = "sglang.srt.layers.attention.flashattention_backend"
+
+
+class TestMLACPDispatch(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_zigzag_cp_prefill_is_one_launch_per_layer(self):
+        """FA MLA under zigzag CP calls the kernel once per layer with the
+        combined geometry and the duplicated page table."""
+        strategy = ZigzagCPStrategy(cp_size=2)
+        with get_parallel().override(attn_cp_rank=0):
+            cp_meta = strategy.build_metadata(8, [8], [8])
+        layer = SimpleNamespace(
+            layer_id=0,
+            head_dim=5,
+            v_head_dim=3,
+            tp_q_head_num=2,
+            tp_k_head_num=1,
+            sliding_window_size=-1,
+            is_cross_attention=False,
+            attn_type=None,
+            scaling=0.5,
+            logit_cap=0.0,
+        )
+        page_table = torch.arange(8, dtype=torch.int32).view(1, 8)
+        backend = FlashAttentionBackend.__new__(FlashAttentionBackend)
+        backend.__dict__.update(
+            use_mla=True,
+            fa_impl_ver=3,
+            device="cpu",
+            page_size=1,
+            num_splits=0,
+            topk=0,
+            local_attn_builder=None,
+            use_sliding_window_kv_pool=False,
+            kv_cache_is_mxfp8=False,
+            token_to_kv_pool=SimpleNamespace(
+                get_key_buffer=lambda _: torch.zeros(16, 1, 5)
+            ),
+            prepare_paged_mha_query=lambda q, qr, kr, *a, **k: (q, qr, kr, None, None),
+            forward_metadata=FlashAttentionMetadata(
+                page_table=page_table, zigzag_page_table=page_table.repeat(2, 1)
+            ),
+        )
+        batch = SimpleNamespace(
+            batch_size=1,
+            forward_mode=ForwardMode.EXTEND,
+            attn_attend_prefix_cache=None,
+            attn_cp_metadata=cp_meta,
+        )
+        q = torch.arange(4 * 2 * 3, dtype=torch.float32).view(4, 2, 3)
+        calls = []
+
+        def attention(**kwargs):
+            calls.append(kwargs)
+            return kwargs["qv"] + 1
+
+        with (
+            patch(f"{MODULE}.is_cp_active", return_value=True),
+            patch(f"{MODULE}.get_cp_strategy", return_value=strategy),
+            patch(f"{MODULE}.flash_attn_with_kvcache", side_effect=attention),
+        ):
+            for _ in range(2):  # two layers
+                out = backend.forward_extend(
+                    q, None, None, layer, batch, q_rope=torch.zeros(4, 2, 2)
+                )
+                torch.testing.assert_close(out, (q + 1).view(4, -1))
+        self.assertEqual(len(calls), 2)
+        for call in calls:
+            self.assertIs(
+                call["page_table"], backend.forward_metadata.zigzag_page_table
+            )
+            self.assertIs(call["cu_seqlens_q"], cp_meta.cu_seqlens_q_combined_tensor)
+            self.assertIs(call["cache_seqlens"], cp_meta.kv_len_combined_tensor)
+            self.assertNotIn("cu_seqlens_k_new", call)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend. Reverts must use GitHub's default format: Revert "original title". Use one space between fields and after the colon, with a non-empty title and no leading or trailing whitespace. Examples: "[Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing", "[Feat] qwen3: Add model support", "[Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance".
